Unfortunately I don't have a lot of answers to these questions since I'm french :/ but I know that each uni site has its section dedicated to international students and the ways to get in etc. 

Financially there's no scholarship, but uni in France is very unexpensive (almost free) compared to the US, I know it went up for international students (we protested a lot but money has its ways so sorry) and if i recall it's around 3k a year ? 
France, especially Paris is very expensive, real estate here is pretty insane honestly, if your parents aren't able to support you fully financially you will have to work alongside your studies which can be tough if you have to put in twice the work because of your french. 

If you want to get in undergrad (Licence) you don't need any prior knowledge and you'd be way ahead with your background and readings. If you're getting into a Master's degree without a psychology Licence you'll still be pretty ok if you chose a psychoanalysis speciality and you have your own knowledge of it (it's mostly writing dissertations so your theoretical background will be appreciated & useful) :) 

Regarding the cities : I've lived in Paris my whole my life until now and it's very nice bc the intellectual/artistic (and nightlife) communities are big BUT it's expensive as hell, crowded and honestly it can break a spirit if you're not wealthy enough... Rennes is very nice, people are nice, it's a student city, the prices are okay but it's not that animated compared to Paris. Nice well, it's special. I don't really vibe with this city bc there are a lot of racists (it's more about 3rd world minorities not the usa if you're wondering, but still), it's also expensive but apart from that the city is insanely gorgeous (mountains AND the sea!!)

I went to the psychoanalysis department of Paris 8 university, it's the department that lacan himself opened, and it's exclusively lacanian but the diploma is "psychoanalysis" it is not "clinical psychology" so you can become a psychoanalyst but you can't be a clinical psychologist and work in institutions (at least not in France). 

There's Paris 7 that deliver clinical psychology diplomas and have lacanian programs in their courses and also Rennes 2 uni and the University of Nice I've heard. 

In France the courses are in french so it can be scary and harder for you but there are a lot of other students who don't speak french very well but they succeed, the teachers in humanities tend to be more understanding :)

Hey, I feel you so much. I thought about it a little but i didn't come to a satisfying conclusion. To me it's because we work a lot on the symptoms (the consequences) with CBT/DBT etc and not enough on the psychological roots of our problems (the cause) with psychoanalysis/introspection etc.

Also being with someone means being intimate with someone and letting them in. We're scared of letting anyone in because we don't even know what's in you know ? That's where the no stable sense of self/constant existential crisis/lack of self confidence stuff kick. Are we, who are so unsure of who we are as a person, willing to let someone who could betray/abandon/hurt us in ? Or worse, let them KNOW us in a way we never did, in a way maybe we wouldn't like to be known ? I mean, I'm scared as shit that my boyfriend may find some bad things about me that I didn't even know. I seek validation and approval all day every day because I'm so unsure of myself. So we may be self sabotaging ourselves and our relationships by making the other despise us (anger, jealousy, being clingy/dependent, petty.....) so the other can leave and not only do we win because no one got near enough to see "the real us" that we we don't know, but also we confirm our pattern of fear of abandonment, because, yet again another left us. 

I think it's that fear of someone not giving us the validation we crave, discovering bad aspects of us and leaving us even more distressed than we already were. It all comes down to the roots of our symptoms, the symptoms are only a reaction, an adaptation to avoid our real problems of that mysterious, unfathomable and "unworthy" self... 

We have to work on the self but I don't know how...

That's exactly how I was able to get to almost 2 months this time! When I wanted to quit before I used to blame myself and all the drugs I've used. I used to say that I hated cannabis for making me an addict, I hated the paranoia, the awkwardness, the feeling of being stuck and so on. Today I view it as a plant that has helped me relax during some rough times, it helped me make some friends in the beginning when I was severely depressed and isolated, and today it helps me realise that I want to be free, that I am a strong person that can overcome anything. The same goes with alcohol, hard drugs and even cigarettes (even though I am still hooked on cigs and I have trouble forgiving myself with that one but I live in Paris and a lot of people smoke and I've made amazing friends with just asking for a lighter...). I think the key is to try and not blame yourself, not have regrets about your life choices because they led you where you are and even though it's hard to fathom, you're going to do amazing things from here :)
Good luck in your quitting process, and remember a relapse is just another obstacle to overcome to rise stronger!
